name: Selected photos access
plain: Lets the user share only chosen photos and videos with the app.
meaning: A narrower grant than full library access. Android 14 lets people pick specific items; Android 16 pre-selects app-owned photos.

android.prompt_ui: Select photos and videos, Allow all, Don't allow
android.persistence: Until revoked; selection can lapse when the app closes
android.revocation: Settings > Apps > Permissions > Photos and videos
android.store_policy: Play: allowed alongside READ_MEDIA_IMAGES; photo picker preferred
android.note: Android 16: when the user limits access, app-owned photos are pre-selected in the picker.

ios.note: Apps can prompt to extend the selection.

limits.headline: Can open only the photos and videos you choose to share, not your whole library
limits.user_action: You tap Select photos and videos (Android) or Select Photos (iPhone) in the prompt
can: Open the specific photos and videos you picked
Let you add more to the shared set later through a prompt
Keep access to those picks until you change them
Find photos the app saved itself, pre-selected on Android 16
cannot: See other photos in your library
See your whole library unless you tap Allow all or Allow Full Access
Change which photos are shared without you
Guess what is in photos you did not share
limits.differs: Both phones offer limited sharing. Android 16 pre-selects photos the app owns; iPhone lets apps prompt to extend the selection.

story.what_it_is: Lets you share only the photos and videos you pick, not the whole gallery.

marketing.name: Partial photo and video access
marketing.pitch: Android 14 notes: users can grant an app access to only the photos and videos they select.

story.for_you: When the app asks for photos you can choose Select photos and pick a few. The app sees only those. It is a safer choice, and you can change it later in Settings.
story.for_makers: Makers can get a post or an upload done without scary full access, which builds trust. The app must handle seeing fewer items than usual.

use_cases.example: You share three photos with a post app and it cannot see the other ones.
A returns app takes one photo of a damaged item and nothing else.
A chat app sends the photos you pick and does not read the rest.
A photo editor works on your chosen pictures only.
A bank app takes one picture of a check from your gallery.
A game uses one photo as your avatar picture.
A dating app lets you pick profile photos without showing the rest.

risks: Apps may keep asking for more
story.android_note: Android 14 adds the option, and Android 16 can preselect photos the app made.
story.ios_note: iOS offers this as Limited Access in the Photos permission.

technical_bounds: Android 14 apps targeting 34+ should handle partial grants

abuse: Pressuring users to grant full access

history.change: Partial photo and video access introduced
Pre-selection of app-owned photos in the limited picker
